in: Migration V12 (additive): on devices (or a device_identity table if cleaner) the recorded identity per contract section 4.3 (CP: SSH host-key fingerprint + observed hostname; PAN: serial + TLS certificate identity), the facts read at first contact (hostname, model, software version, HA role), the identity-mismatch warning state (open/none) with the management plane's last view, and the C4 section 4.2 modifiers cluster_member_ref / virtual_system_ref as columns or a small table; C1 section 3.5 audit trigger attached. No VS- or cluster-scoped devices row ever (CP-D6).

The confirm as a C4 read capability (EC-12): one capability per vendor whose steps are connect -> identity read -> HA/peer read -> disconnect, each command/route string declared ONCE in a closed set mirroring DEVICE_FIRST_CONTACT_COMMAND_GATE_ENTRIES.md entries 1-4 (a test asserts the set equals the table). Executed in the worker through the existing transports and the store-backed resolvers (CS-3); credential resolution failure refuses before any contact (SB-16).

Service: POST /devices/add-single {address, vendor, credential_reference_id} -- role:onboarding_admin's enrollment confirm (C3 section 4.1, B1_04B section 3) -- creates the DRAFT row, runs the confirm capability, and on completion lands ENROLLED with the read facts and the recorded identity (EC-6a: also when identity differs from an earlier record -- warn+audit+continue, ID-M1..ID-M3); the request returns the row and the outcome (facts read / UNKNOWN fields / peer outcome). The strict-refuse posture switch of 13F ID-M3 is a property, default off, honoured here.

Peer follow (PF-1..PF-5): if the HA read names a peer AND carries its management address, contact that peer once with the same credential, run the same two reads, and form the unit only if the peer names the first device back -- then create the peer's rows and set cluster_member_ref on both to one opaque unit id. If the address is absent, the peer unreachable, or the claim one-sided: record 'peer named, not confirmed' on the first device and stop. Never a second hop, never a VIP as a target (13F CL-1), never another credential.

Frontend: AddDeviceDialog becomes real -- address, vendor (Check Point / Palo Alto), credential (select from GET /credentials), then two buttons: 'Single device' (this movement) and 'Management server (discovery)' (present but disabled with the plain text 'next step', DA-3 is the following movement). Submit shows progress (connecting, reading identity, checking peer) and the result: the device row with its read facts, the peer outcome, and any identity-mismatch warning with the management plane's view beside it (contract section 6). Inventory screen lists devices with hostname, vendor, model, version, HA role, enrollment state, and the cluster as a parent row grouping its members (SB-9). No liveness vocabulary anywhere (LV-1 carried over).

Tests, first two written FIRST and observed failing: (1) the peer-follow corroboration rule -- a one-sided claim forms no unit, a reciprocal one does, over a fake transport; (2) the closed command set equals the gate table and nothing else is ever sent. Then: refusal before contact on an unresolvable credential; ENROLLED landing with UNKNOWN facts when the read is unparseable; identity mismatch warns and continues by default, refuses when the posture switch is on; no VIP is ever a ConnectionTarget; existing registration, discovery and credential-store tests stay green; frontend dialog test.

unresolved_risks: ARCHITECTURE GAP (the main blocker for AC-3/AC-5): Ui2ArchitectureTest.dir2_web_cannot_reach_worker_or_transport_implementations hard-forbids any class in the `service` package from depending on any class in the `worker` package -- and this session's confirm engine necessarily lives in `worker` (it uses SshExecTransport/PanXmlApiTransport/the store-backed credential resolvers directly, per WORKER.md's own instruction). No worker-side daemon or poll loop exists anywhere in production code today (StepExecutor -- the one class that already drives a Capability's steps against a DeviceTransport -- is constructed only in job-engine's own unit tests; grep confirms no production caller). So a POST /devices/add-single that both creates the DRAFT row from :service AND runs the confirm from the same request, in the same process, cannot be built without either (a) violating DIR-2, or (b) building new cross-process infrastructure. Two options for the PO/architecture owner to choose between, not decided unilaterally here: (1) async -- :service admits a job via the already-built JobAdmissionService/job-engine, a new small worker-side entry point (mirroring the existing DiscoveryRunnerMain pattern) claims and executes it via ConfirmCapabilityExecutor, :service polls the devices row for a bounded window and returns whatever state it finds (matches the frontend brief's own 'submit shows progress' language); (2) relax DIR-2 for this one narrow case with an explicit architecture amendment, which the FROZEN Ui2ArchitectureTest itself would need to accept as authorized scope creep -- not something a single implementation movement should do to its own gate test.
